title: Engineering Manager - Data Platform
text:
Within the Data Platform studio, we own two critical pillars: our event delivery platform that collects trillions of events per day from producers to consumers, and another, which handles the pseudonymisation of data so Spotify can use data responsibly and in compliance with privacy regulations. These systems sit at the heart of Spotify's data collection and are used by hundreds of teams across the company.

 We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a team of six experienced engineers distributed across Europe. You'll set the technical direction, ensure the team delivers high-impact work, and - just as importantly - invest deeply in the growth and careers of your engineers. If you're energised by both the technical challenges of large-scale data systems and the human side of building a high-performing team, we'd love to hear from you.
What You’ll Do
- Lead and develop a team of six experienced engineers, with a strong focus on coaching, career development, and creating an environment where people do the best work of their careers.

- Take accountability for the team's delivery, ensuring clear priorities, healthy execution, and measurable outcomes.

- Partner with product and stakeholders to shape the roadmap for event delivery and privacy infrastructure.

- Drive technical strategy and architectural decisions for systems operating at Spotify scale.

- Build a culture of ownership, psychological safety, and continuous improvement.

- Collaborate across Data Platform and the wider engineering organisation to align on shared goals and dependencies.

- Manage on-call health, operational excellence, and reliability for the team's services.

- Actively participate in hiring, onboarding, and growing the team's capabilities.
Who You Are
- You have experience managing teams of senior/experienced engineers and understand that people leadership is your primary craft, not a side responsibility.

- You have a track record of investing in engineers' careers - running meaningful development conversations, helping people grow into new roles, and creating clarity around expectations and progression.

- You're comfortable with distributed data systems, event-driven architectures, or data infrastructure at scale - you don't need to write the code, but you can engage credibly in technical discussions and unblock your team.

- You hold yourself and your team accountable for outcomes, not just activity.

- You communicate clearly and build trust across functions and time zones.

- You've worked with distributed teams and understand how to create cohesion and inclusion when people aren't in the same room.

- You're excited about the potential of AI and LLMs to transform how engineering teams work - whether that's accelerating development workflows, rethinking how data infrastructure is built and operated, or helping your team adopt AI-assisted tooling effectively.
Where You’ll Be
- This role is based in London.

- We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

title: Engineering Manager - Experimentation
text:
Think it, build it, ship it, tweak it" is at the core of Spotify's product development approach. In the Experimentation product area we are providing Spotify and external customers with Confidence, our platform to quickly and safely iterate through ideas, learn from them and make informed decisions for better products.
 
At Spotify, experimentation touches almost all of our functions from marketing via content management to consumer products, and we’re running several thousands of tests every year. Through confidence, we 're sharing all our findings and practices with more companies as a commercial SaaS product.
 
The team you will manage is a skilled and highly engaged group of engineers that are distributed over Europe. As an Engineering manager, you coach them individually and as a team, maintaining their strong team culture and helping them thrive and and grow. Your technical experience provides mentorship and guidelines to the team, which ensures quality and timeliness of your deliveries. Your leadership promotes creativity, collaboration and courage, which forms a kind and productive team with a high bar for quality and pace of delivery.

What You'll Do
- You will hire, coach and develop the careers of a team of engineers

- You will be responsible for high-quality deliveries

- You will partner with product managers to support with prioritizations and product visions

- You will support the engineering team and work with Staff engineers to formulate the technical strategy needed to deliver on our vision

- You will do hands on engineering work from time to time

- In the end, your primary goal is to support a highly effective engineering team delivering an amazing product
Who You Are
- You thrive when developing great people, not just great products and cultivating a strong engineering culture in an agile environment

- You are skilled in collaborating on and developing distributed systems that can scale to millions of users.

- You have experience with data warehouses and data processing at scale

- You have worked on commercial SaaS products in the past and have hands on experience taking features from zero to one

- You are a brave learner and see unfamiliar territories as an opportunity to grow.

- You are a senior individual contributor (or has been) with strong people skills and leadership experience

- You’re passionate about software engineering best practices and love to have an impact on large-scale tech problems

- You care deeply about quality of the products your working and, and hold people to a high standard

- Naturally, you harness AI as a tool that helps you be more effective at your work
Where You'll Be 
- Based in Stockholm, Sweden

- We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home. We ask that you come in 3 times per week.

title: Engineering Manager - Subscriptions
text:
At Spotify, our Subscriptions organisation helps listeners discover the value of Spotify, find the right subscription, and keep enjoying the content they love. From acquisition and activation to retention, commerce, and customer service, we build experiences that connect listeners with Spotify and support lasting relationships.
We're looking for an Engineering Manager II to lead a team of data and backend engineers within our Subscriptions Mission. Your team will build data products, pipelines, and services that help teams understand listener needs and deliver more relevant experiences. You'll work closely with product managers, data scientists, business partners, and engineers to turn complex challenges into reliable solutions. You'll also create an environment where engineers can grow, collaborate, and make a meaningful impact.

What You'll Do

 Lead, support, and develop a team of data and backend engineers, creating an inclusive environment where everyone can contribute and grow.

- 
 Work with product managers, business partners, and engineering teams to set priorities and build data products that improve the subscription experience.

-

-

-

-

- 
 Explore opportunities to use AI and automation to simplify workflows, improve data quality, and support your team's work.
Who You Are
- 
 You have experience leading data or backend engineering teams and enjoy helping engineers develop their skills and careers.

- 
 You have a background in software or data engineering and can guide technical discussions about data architecture, distributed systems, scalability, and reliability.

- 
 You understand how to balance team development, technical decisions, and delivery priorities to achieve meaningful results.

- 
 You have worked with large-scale data pipelines, data platforms, or backend services. Experience with technologies such as Google Cloud, BigQuery, Apache Beam, Dataflow, dbt, Flyte, Airflow, Scala, or Java is valuable.

- 
 You can navigate changing priorities, make informed decisions, and help your team move forward when the path isn't always clear.

- 
 You communicate clearly and build effective partnerships with product, business, and engineering teams to turn shared goals into practical solutions.

- 
 You value different perspectives, encourage open feedback, and help create an environment where people feel respected and supported.

- 
 You're curious about new technologies, including AI and automation, and enjoy finding ways to improve how teams work and deliver value.
Where You'll Be
- 
 We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! For this role, you can be within the EMEA region as long as we have a work location (excluding France due to on-call restrictions).

- 
 This team operates within the Central European and GMT time zone for collaboration.

title: Machine Learning Engineer - Subscriptions
text:
At Spotify, our Subscriptions Mission focuses on creating experiences that help listeners discover the value of Spotify, become subscribers, and stay with us for the long term. By combining technology, experimentation, and a deep understanding of our users, we help connect artists and fans while building a sustainable subscription business.

 Within the Subscriptions Mission, the Subs Foundational Models Product Area is part of the Subs User Understanding Studio. We build scalable machine learning solutions that personalize the subscriber journey, from conversion through to long-term retention. Working closely with teams across the mission, we develop ML solutions that improve key business metrics, including subscriber growth, monthly active users, and Premium retention.

 We're looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to join our Radius squad. You'll take ownership of impactful ML initiatives, develop and improve production models, and contribute to the foundational ML capabilities that power personalization and optimization across Subscriptions.

 Your work could include reducing friction for Free users while balancing retention and conversion, improving payment experiences to reduce Premium churn, or developing reusable models such as subscriber embeddings that support multiple products and use cases.
What You'll Do
- Lead multi-week ML initiatives end to end, from translating business requirements into technical specifications to shipping models and measuring their impact on subscriber metrics

- Own components of our ML systems, making independent technical trade-offs and keeping them observable, reliable, and well documented

- Collaborate with a multi-functional agile team spanning user research, design, data science, product management, and engineering to build new product features that advance our mission to connect artists and fans in personalised and relevant ways

- Prototype new approaches and productionise solutions at scale for our hundreds of millions of active users

- Help drive optimisation, testing, and tooling to improve quality

- Unblock and share context with your teammates to raise the whole squad's velocity

- Use AI-assisted engineering to move faster and remove repetitive toil, while owning the quality of everything you ship

- Partner closely with senior and staff ML engineers, and be part of an active group of machine learning practitioners in your mission and across Spotify
Who You Are
- You have experience building and shipping production ML systems

- You have a strong background in machine learning, theory, and practice

- You are comfortable explaining the intuition and assumptions behind ML concepts

- You can own well-scoped ML projects end to end and make sound technical decisions independently

- You communicate clearly with stakeholders and can explain the reasoning behind your technical choices

- You are curious, open to feedback, and keen to grow your scope over time

- You have hands-on experience implementing and maintaining production ML systems in Python, Scala, or similar languages, including model development with PyTorch

- You are experienced with building data pipelines, and you are self-sufficient in getting the data you need to build and evaluate your models

- You preferably have experience with cloud platforms like GCP or AWS

- You care about agile software processes, data development, reliability, and focused experimentation

- You have a desire to drive business impact

title: Abuse Research Engineer
text:
Who we are

 About Stripe

 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. 

 About the team

 Abuse Research Group (ARG) handles proactive threat hunting and adversary behavior analysis across Stripe products. Rather than reacting to alerts, the team maps end-to-end fraud and abuse paths, validates novel attack vectors, and identifies product conditions that enable fraud. Using agentic automated testing and simulation tools, ARG translates research into actionable threat advisories, strategic control recommendations, and regression scenarios to systematically eliminate vulnerabilities.

 What you’ll do

 As an Abuse Research Engineer in the Abuse Research Group, you will play a critical role in safeguarding Stripe’s financial ecosystem by proactively hunting for advanced threats, dissecting complex fraud vectors, and extracting actionable adversary intelligence.  Rather than relying solely on reactive alerts, you will develop and execute hypothesis-driven threat hunting operations across internal telemetry and external sources to uncover fraudulent tools, tactics, and techniques (TTPs) before they impact Stripe’s platform. Central to this work is FT3 (Fraud Taxonomy 3.0), Stripe’s multi-layered taxonomy that decomposes monolithic fraud into structured kill chains.  Collaborating cross-functionally with Fraud Ops, Strategy, Risk, Onboarding, and Security, you will integrate threat intelligence, build agentic simulation workflows, and systematically eliminate product vulnerabilities.

 Responsibilities

- Proactive Threat Hunting & Kill Chain Analysis: Formulate hypotheses and conduct iterative threat hunting operations across Stripe systems and external data.

- FT3 Taxonomy: Apply and enrich the FT3 framework across empirical datasets and incidents, standardizing threat intelligence across kill chain phases and targeted API endpoints.  

- Threat Intelligence & Signal Expansion: Partner with teams like Fraud Intelligence to integrate, curate, and automate threat feeds into engineering workflows.  

- Cross-Functional Advisories & Strategic Controls: Translate raw research and retrospective findings into actionable threat advisories and control recommendations (policy, technical systems, support workflows, and detection mechanisms) for stakeholders across Fraud, Risk, Onboarding, and Security.  

- Agentic Testing & Adversary Simulation: Utilize agentic automated testing frameworks to simulate adversary TTPs, validate whether deployed controls interrupt empirical kill chains, and generate regression scenarios to exercise controls.  

 Who you are 

 We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. 

 Minimum requirements

- 5+ years of experience conducting threat intelligence, threat hunting, or technical incident response within cyber security, product abuse, or trust domains.  

- 5+ years of experience analyzing large, complex datasets using data analytics tools to identify anomalies, map behavioral trends, and solve complex fraud problems.  

- B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.  

- Expert proficiency in Python and SQL, with demonstrated experience using code and scripting to automate workflows, build investigative tools, or query big data pipelines.  

- Hands-on experience in log analysis (e.g., application logs, API route telemetry, network security events), digital forensics, and cyber investigation methodologies.  

- Strong communication skills with a proven ability to translate complex technical research into clear, actionable recommendations and advisories for cross-functional partners.

 Preferred qualifications 

- Deep technical understanding of threat actor motivations, infrastructure, and TTPs specific to financial fraud (e.g., ATO, Card Testing, Credential Stuffing). 

- Familiarity with standardized taxonomies such as FT3 or MITRE ATT&CK.  

- Proficiency with engineering, data processing, and analysis platforms such as Databricks, Trino, PySpark, Pandas, or Scikit-Learn.  

- Proven background utilizing Threat Intelligence Platforms (TIPs), tactical threat feeds, OSINT, and breach intelligence. 

- Demonstrated capability building or leveraging agentic LLM tools, automated testing systems, or control validation frameworks to model adversary behavior at scale.  

- Participation in industry conferences, webinars, or threat-sharing groups, alongside relevant professional certifications (e.g., GCTI, GCFA, OSCP).
